gold_assessment.reasoning: Generated hpi-001 captures a 5-day history of feeling run down with cough; wording differs slightly ('generally unwell' vs 'run down') but core facts align.
Generated hpi-001 states 'mostly dry cough', which corresponds to 'mainly dry cough'; extra details about timing/productivity are additions.
Generated hpi-004 notes mild SOB without chest pain or tightness, matching 'No chest pain. Feeling more SOB.'

Gold specifies feeling hot/cold and sweaty with no fevers. Generated hpi-005 instead reports intermittent fevers/chills and nocturnal sweating, which conflicts regarding presence of fever; the afebrile aspect is not captured.

Runny nose and sore throat are reflected in generated hpi-001 (mucus component loosely) and hpi-002 (runny nose, sore throat). Blocked ears are not explicitly mentioned; generated hpi-003 notes mild ear discomfort, which is related but not identical to 'blocked ears'.

Gold mentions myalgia and arthralgia (joint stiffness). Generated hpi-007 mentions stiffness in elbows and knees with movement but does not link this to myalgia/arthralgia; it reframes it anatomically without referencing generalized myalgia/arthralgia. The specific diagnosis terms are omitted.
Generated hpi-006 states initial mild diarrhea that has resolved, matching 'diarrhea but resolved.'
No generated fact mentions absence of unwell contacts or absence of nausea/vomiting.
Generated pmh-001 and pmh-002 cover type 2 diabetes and hypertension. Obesity is not mentioned in any generated fact, so that component is omitted.
Generated med-001 and med-003 cover metformin and aspirin. Lisinopril is not identified; instead, an 'unspecified second med' is used, which does not explicitly state lisinopril.
No generated facts address drug allergies or NKDA.

Generated sh-003 and sh-004 state patient lives with wife and works in a local factory; this corresponds to living with wife and working in factory/manufacturing. Extra detail of 'steel parts' is additive.

Gold: smoking socially and >9 units/week alcohol. Generated sh-001 and sh-002 describe ~9 pints/week and occasional smoking with vaporizer. Smoking and alcohol use are present, but the exact quantity threshold '>9 units/week' is not clearly matched (pints vs units) and vaping detail is additional.

Gold impression is viral URTI/?LRTI. Generated asm-001 states viral URTI with probable early influenza; this is a different diagnostic label (influenza vs possible LRTI) and does not mention possible LRTI, so the specific gold impression is not captured.
Generated plan-001 recommends supportive care with rest, hydration, and paracetamol, aligning with conservative management: rest, fluids, regular paracetamol.

Gold: delayed amoxicillin to start in 24–48 hours if symptoms not improving. Generated med-004/plan-002: delayed amoxicillin to start if symptoms worsen or SOB persists beyond 24–48 hours. Timing is consistent; the trigger condition (worsening/persistent SOB vs 'not improving') is modified, so only partially aligned.
Gold: review in one week if not better. Generated plan-003 and fu-001: return if no improvement or worsening after one week; this matches.
Gold adds advice to seek earlier review for worsening symptoms including chest pain, SOB, or fevers. No generated fact specifies earlier-than-one-week review for these specific red-flag symptoms.

gen_assessment.reasoning: 5-day history of feeling unwell with cough is supported by gold hpi-001 and hpi-002. Added details (worse in AM, occasional mucus) are not in gold but not contradictory.
Runny nose and sore throat are supported by gold hpi-005. Hoarseness related to shouting at football is not mentioned in gold and is an addition.
Gold mentions 'blocked ears' but not 'mild ear discomfort' or hearing loss. This is a related but distinct symptom description not specified in gold; no contradiction.
Mild SOB without chest pain or tightness is consistent with 'No chest pain. Feeling more SOB.' in gold hpi-003.
Gold hpi-004: feeling hot/cold and sweaty, no fevers. Generated hpi-005: intermittent fevers/chills and nocturnal sweating, introducing fevers contrary to 'No fevers.'
Initial mild diarrhea that has resolved aligns with 'diarrhea but resolved.' in gold hpi-007; 'mild' is an added qualifier.

Gold hpi-006 notes myalgia and arthralgia with joint stiffness but does not specify elbows and knees or movement-related stiffness. The anatomical and functional specifics are additional detail not present in gold.
Gold pmh-001 includes type 2 diabetes among conditions; generated pmh-001 isolates this diagnosis, which is consistent but incomplete relative to all comorbidities.
Gold pmh-001 includes hypertension; generated pmh-002 correctly reflects this condition.
Metformin is listed in gold med-001; generated med-001 matches this medication.

Gold specifies lisinopril explicitly. Generated med-002 refers to an 'unspecified second medication' without naming it; this is less specific and not directly supported by gold wording, but does not contradict it. It is treated as an incomplete/additional formulation rather than supported.
Gold med-001: aspirin (no frequency qualifier). Generated med-003: aspirin taken occasionally. The use of aspirin is supported; the 'occasional' frequency is added detail not in gold.

Gold plan-002: delayed amoxicillin to start in 24–48 hours if symptoms not improving. Generated med-004: start if symptoms worsen or SOB persists beyond 24–48 hours. Timing is supported; trigger conditions are modified, so only partial support.
Gold: >9 units/week alcohol; generated: ~9 pints/week. Both indicate regular alcohol use, but units vs pints and threshold differ; amount is not directly supported and is an approximation/addition.
Gold sh-002: smoking socially. Generated sh-002: occasional smoking and using vaporizer to cut down. Occasional smoking matches social smoking; vaporizer use is added detail.

Gold sh-001: lives with wife and works in factory/manufacturing. Generated sh-003: lives with wife and no children at home. Living with wife is supported; the absence of children at home is additional information.
Gold: works in factory/manufacturing. Generated: works in local factory making steel parts. Job type matches; 'steel parts' and 'local' are added detail.
No physical exam or call-observed findings are described in gold. Audible sniffles/runny nose noted on call are new details.
Gold does not address documentation completeness of vitals/exam. Statement that no vitals or physical exam were recorded is new meta-documentation information.

Gold asm-001: viral URTI/?LRTI. Generated asm-001: viral URI with probable early influenza features. Introducing influenza features and omitting possible LRTI shifts the diagnostic impression; this differs materially from the gold impression and is not supported.
Gold lists diabetes and hypertension in PMH but does not state they are 'controlled' in assessment. Classification as controlled T2DM and HTN is additional interpretive information.

Gold hpi-003: more SOB and no chest pain. Generated asm-003: mild SOB without chest pain and low suspicion for bacterial pneumonia. SOB without chest pain is supported; the assessment of low suspicion for bacterial pneumonia is an added evaluative detail.
Supportive care with rest, hydration, and paracetamol matches conservative management (rest, fluids, regular paracetamol) in gold plan-001.
Same as med-004: delayed amoxicillin and 24–48 hour window align with gold; initiation criteria (worsen/persistent SOB vs not improving) differ, so only partial support.
Return if no improvement or worsening after one week matches gold follow-up instruction: review in one week if not better (with an added explicit mention of worsening).
Gold mentions smoking habits but does not include smoking cessation advice. Encouraging smoking cessation and vaporizer use is new plan content.
Gold PMH lists diabetes and HTN but plan does not mention monitoring. Routine monitoring of diabetes and BP is new management content.
Instruction to return if no improvement or worsening after one week is consistent with gold 'Review in 1/52 if not better'; explicit mention of worsening is additional nuance.
